The Empty Seat at the Hearing

听证会上的空座位 · 647 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1An elected council wanted to reform the use of an old market hall. A private company offered to turn it into a shopping center. A citizens' initiative proposed a public study room instead. The mayor called a hearing during an election campaign. Both parties treated the hall as a symbol of their policy. Mira, a deputy on the advisory committee, noticed that the agenda gave time to each political group but no seat to the pupils who used the hall after school. She asked the chairperson to leave one place open.

2The committee had advisory authority under a local provision. A legislative officer said only the elected council could decide by a majority. An opposition representative demanded a vote. A conservative favored a commission, while a liberal wanted public consultation. Mira proposed a forum in accordance with the constitution. Its procedures would feel inclusive only if minority residents could take part. A teacher told her that democracy should be visible at this small meeting, even though it would never make the agenda of parliament.

3A delegation from the traders protested. Its outgoing chairman said the plan might abolish cheap stalls. A student took the empty seat and showed where pupils waited. She had no membership in a party and made no claim to speak on behalf of all pupils. A civic activist praised her factual evidence. A nationalist member tried to make the dispute about ethnic identity. The chairperson asked all sides to put their respective proposals on the same map. A divisive speech did not show how the hall could be shared.

4The compromise kept the stalls and opened an upper room. A planning officer noted a second exit was required by legislation. A prominent councilor wanted the result announced before the ballot. An official warned the mayor that he might have to veto a plan that defied a safety rule. In the recess a moderate member proposed moving the entrance. The contentious detail turned out to be crucial. It satisfied the provision and created a basis for consensus.

5A politician then urged the council to put only the original choices on the ballot. It would favor his party's candidacy. A voter accused him of trying to sway opinion before a midterm contest. Mira said costs should be published. The mayor appointed an independent officer to hear objections. This consultative step took time. It also made the eventual decision accountable to supporters, critics, and people who simply preferred a clearer explanation to another campaign slogan.

6The debate was followed by a conference of neighborhood groups. A progressive activist criticized the administration. A republican and a socialist agreed that it had ignored the stairs. A former minister who attended as a resident asked the council to publish its ruling and explain how it planned to govern the shared hall. One supporter feared public criticism would become overwhelming. Mira said that an open explanation was preferable to a formality whose result everyone learned from a poster.

7The council adopted the compromise after deliberation. One member expressed disapproval and another abstained. The decisive majority accepted the resolution, while the mayor agreed to implement it after the safety work. Mira asked the advisory committee to include a student delegate on its review agenda. It was a small change in representation. The student would have a regular opportunity to check whether the new schedule fulfilled the public promise.

8At opening the room had two entrances and six tables. A reporter called it a victory for democracy. Mira asked him to write about a choice people could verify. A congressional or senate debate would draw more attention. Here the contested proposition concerned a law about safety and a room used after school. She showed him the stalls below and the posted hours above. A resident who had publicly opposed the original plan came in with a book. The student sat beside him.

四级汇总词汇 · 22中文译文

听证会上的空座位

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1民选议会想改变旧市场大厅的用途。一家公司想把它变成购物中心，市民发起的提案则想办公共自习室。市长在竞选期间开听证会，双方都把大厅当成自己政策的象征。咨询委员会副手米拉发现，议程给各政治团体都留了时间，却没有座位给放学后使用大厅的学生。她请主持人空出一个位置。

2按地方规定，委员会有咨询权。立法官员说，只有民选议会才能按多数票决定。反对派代表要求投票，保守派倾向设委员会，自由派则主张先问市民。米拉提议依照宪法开公共论坛。少数群体居民也能发言，程序才有包容性。一位老师对她说，哪怕这件事不会进入国会议程，人们也应该能在这样的小会议上看见民主。

3商贩代表团提出抗议。即将卸任的主席怕方案撤掉便宜摊位。一名学生坐上空位，指给大家看孩子们在哪里等候。她没加入政党，也不代表所有学生。一名市民活动人士称赞她拿出了事实。有人想把争论引到族群身份上，主席要求各方把各自的方案画在同一张图上。分裂人群的演说，说明不了大厅怎样共用。

4折中办法保留摊位，开放楼上一间屋。规划人员指出，法律要求另设一个出口。一位知名议员想在投票前公布结果，官员提醒市长，违反安全规定的方案也许必须否决。休会期间，一名立场温和的委员提议换入口。大家争的这个细节恰好是关键。既满足规定，也给各方达成共识留下空间。

5有政客接着要求，选票只列最初的两个选项。这对他所在党的候选人有利。一位选民质疑他想在中期竞选前左右意见。米拉说，应公开成本。市长任命独立人员听取反对意见。协商占了一些时间，却让最终决定能对支持者、批评者和只想听懂事情的人负责。

6辩论后，社区团体又开了一场会。一名进步人士批评行政部门忽略楼梯，一名共和派和一名社会主义者也同意。前部长以居民身份出席，请议会公布裁定，解释如何管理共用大厅。一位支持者怕公开批评会太多。米拉说，公开说明，总比大家只从一张海报得知结果的走过场好。

7议会讨论后采纳折中办法。一人表示不赞成，另一人弃权，多数明确接受决议。市长同意安全工程完工后实施。米拉让咨询委员会把学生代表列入复审议程。这是代表权的一点变化，学生能定期检查新时间表有没有兑现对公众的承诺。

8开放时，屋里有两个入口和六张桌。一位记者称它是民主的胜利。米拉请他写一个人们能核实的决定。国会或参议院辩论会更吸引眼球，这里的争议却围绕安全法规和一间放学后可用的屋。她指给记者看楼下的摊位和楼上贴的开放时间。曾公开反对原方案的居民拿着书进来，那名学生坐到他旁边。
